description.value: An fMRI study comparing neural substrates of emotional versus non-emotional conflict modulation by global control context using face-word interference tasks with manipulated proportion congruent blocks and an independent face localizer.

quotes: We addressed this aim in a functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study that varied the proportion of congruent trials in emotional vs. non-emotional conflict tasks across blocks.

description.value: Twenty-four right-handed volunteers participated; three were excluded, leaving 21 participants. Participants completed emotional and non-emotional face-word conflict tasks and a subsequent independent face-versus-house localizer during fMRI. Task-domain, current congruency, proportion congruent, and previous-trial congruency were within-subject factors.

quotes: Participants performed two tasks during fMRI: a face-word interference task (including an emotional and a non-emotional version), which was performed first, and a subsequent standard localizer task to provide independent functional definitions of the FFA and the amygdala as ROIs.

description.value: Functional images were slice-time corrected, realigned, coregistered with the structural image, normalized to MNI space, high-pass filtered, and spatially smoothed.

quotes: Functional data were slice-time corrected and spatially realigned to the first volume of the first run. The structural scan was co-registered to the functional images, and served to calculate transformation parameters for spatially warping functional images to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template brain (resampled voxel size: 2 mm ). Finally, normalized functional images were spatially smoothed with an 8 mm  full-width-half-maximum Gaussian kernel. The first 5 volumes of each run were discarded prior to building and estimating the statistical models. In order to remove low-frequency confounds, data were high-pass filtered (128 s).
All preprocessing and statistical analyses were carried out using SPM8 (  http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm/software/spm8/  ).

model_settings.value: Sixteen event regressors crossed task-domain, proportion congruent, previous-trial congruency, and current-trial congruency; error trials, first trials of blocks, and instruction screens were nuisance regressors. Temporal autocorrelation was modeled with AR-1 and restricted maximum likelihood variance-component estimates.

quotes: Regressors for stimulus events (convolved with a canonical hemodynamic response function) were created for each of the combinations of task-domain (emotional vs. non-emotional), proportion congruent (low proportion vs. high proportion), previous trial congruency (incongruent vs. congruent) and current trial congruency (congruent vs. incongruent) factors, resulting in a total of 16 different trial types/regressors. Additionally, we modeled error trials, the first trial of each block, and instruction screens as nuisance regressors. Temporal autocorrelations were estimated using restricted maximum likelihood estimates of variance components using a first-order autoregressive model (AR-1), and the resulting non-sphericity was used to form maximum likelihood estimates of the activations.
This model was applied to each subject's data, followed by linear contrasts between events of interest.
